Disgusting. This place was disgusting and not fit for human habitation. There were no redeeming qualities to speak of. My party arrived to find that our room was not on the nice tower like we were led to believe, but in the shorter, much older tower across the parking lot. Staff was reluctant to let us use a bell cart to transport our belongings across the parking lot. When we arrived on our floor via a poorly maintained and visibility distressed elevator, we were struck by a strong, musky odor, visibly water damaged ceilings, and threadbare carpeting. When we arrived at our room, we were greeted by an even stronger musty odor, water damaged walls that looked like something out of a zombie movie, stains on the sheets, a filthy bathroom, and a mini fridge full of mold. I say again, FULL OF MOLD. The carpet felt moist and the air was quite humid, dispite the AC operating at refrigerator temperatures. The sink did not get warm, and the shower only did when the sink was on. This baffled us. We were unable to get a new room at that time and with other properties in Ft Lauderdale full at the time of our stay, we had little choice but to stay in the horror film set of a room. The next morning, staff were able to get us a room in the newer tower due to a last minute cancellation. They told a member of our party that the old tower was closed for a while and only reopened to accommodate the Ft Lauderdale boat show. Seems they just turned the power on and didn't bother to check any of the rooms. While the new room wasn't moldy (maybe), it was full of ants, had wildly inconsistent shower temperature, had a broken outlet, and still had some water damage. Did I mention the ants?
Staff, especially valet staff, were rude and pushy. One was genuinely upset when we asked for a bell cart to move our belongings to the new room, claiming he would lose his job if we didn't return it. He may have been joking, but his tone did not convey that. He continued to hound us while we waited in the lobby for our new room keys. During the move, the valet staff had to move cars to create an accessable path. They complained about this. Finally, one staff member snapped at a guest in our party when asking them if they would need their car again later in the evening.
On some smaller points, the coffee in the cafe was terrible, the pool was disgusting, the pool area was poorly maintained with broken furniture and empty drink cups left laying around, the pool bar was inadequately staffed and took forever, and the drinks we were given were watered down and not very good.
In conclusion, I have never in my life had a hotel experience as awful as this. The location on the beach is not worth the headache, and especially not worth the price. Hilton, hang your head in shame for allowing this biohazard of a hotel to remain open in this state. I truly believe the old tower is not fit for human habitation. Stay away. Stay far away.

Very Disappointing Stay — Excellent Staff, Unacceptable Room Conditions

We have been loyal Hilton guests for many years, and the Hilton Fort Lauderdale Beach Resort has been one of our favorite properties. Unfortunately, our most recent stay was extremely disappointing.

I want to be very clear that the resort staff was wonderful. Jada at the front desk went above and beyond to help us, and the front desk, restaurant, bell, and valet teams were all friendly, professional, and exceptional. Our concerns are absolutely not a reflection of these employees.

The problem was the condition and cleanliness of the rooms.

We requested an OceanFront room and prefer a high floor. When we entered our first room on the 21st floor, we were shocked to find that the bed had not been properly made and the room was visibly dirty. Jada immediately stepped in and worked hard to find us another room, for which we were very grateful.

Unfortunately, the second room on the 19th floor had significant cleanliness and maintenance issues as well. The sheets had visible stains, there were cup marks and other signs of inadequate cleaning in the kitchen and bathroom, the appliances were dirty, and the floors were so dirty that we began wearing socks rather than walking barefoot. The amount of dirt that accumulated on our socks was honestly shocking.

This was not a matter of expecting perfection. Basic cleanliness and properly maintained accommodations should be a minimum standard at a Hilton resort.

We ultimately decided to stay rather than continue changing rooms and put an even greater burden on the staff, particularly after Jada had already done everything she could to help us. However, encountering substantial cleanliness issues in two separate rooms made it clear to us that this was more than an isolated oversight.

We documented the condition of the rooms with photographs and, on September 21, 2026, sent a detailed complaint directly to Hilton’s President and CEO and customer care dept, along with our customer concern. Unfortunately, we received no response.

That lack of response is especially disappointing because we have always valued Hilton and would much rather continue staying at a property we once considered one of our favorites than have to look elsewhere. We have recently begun exploring other luxury properties in the Fort Lauderdale area, and our experiences elsewhere have been significantly better.

We hope Hilton takes a serious look at housekeeping standards and room inspections at this property. The employees we encountered clearly care about their guests, but even exceptional staff cannot overcome inadequate housekeeping and management standards.

We loved this resort. It is disappointing to now feel that we can no longer rely on it to provide the level of cleanliness and quality we expect from Hilton.

I stayed at this hotel in September and wanted to wait before leaving my review. The hotel did reach out to me and insisted on doing two things to address my concerns. However, they only followed through with one. Since I strongly believe in people keeping their word, I most likely won’t return to give this hotel another try. I do appreciate them reaching out nonetheless.

To start, the front desk receptionist was very nice and allowed me to check in a little early, which I appreciated. The room was decent overall. Although I didn’t get the king room I originally wanted, the receptionist gave me the option to wait or take a double-bed room earlier. I chose the double, which was perfectly fine.

My main concerns were with the room’s cleanliness and maintenance. There was a significant amount of rust around the bathroom sink area, which I believe should have been addressed before assigning the room to a guest. I also noticed several streaks on the trash can near the toilet that appeared to possibly be urine. I can’t say for certain, but regardless, the trash can should have been thoroughly cleaned or replaced for hygiene purposes.

Aside from those issues, the hotel appeared to be in a decent location, and I had no trouble getting around using Uber. I am also a solo black woman traveler and I felt very safe in the hotel and with staff.

Overall, the staff was pleasant, and the room was decent, but the cleanliness concerns and the hotel’s failure to follow through on everything they promised left me disappointed. Those were my main issues, and unfortunately, they are enough to make me reconsider staying here again.
